Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replay browser physics

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

export.py runs the ordinary Dockyard SDK build, editor import and official Web export. browser.py serves that immutable export with isolation headers and runs two independent Chrome processes against the existing local RTC signalling fixture. The relay carries SDP/ICE and room membership; game traffic uses real WebRTC data channels and the existing Replay Session, complete codec and Timeline.

Shell
python3 -B tests/box3d_web/replay/export.py \
  --out "$NEW_EXPORT" --native-library "$NATIVE_LIBRARY" \
  --web-archive "$WEB_ARCHIVE" --odin "$ODIN" --godot "$GODOT" --emcc "$EMCC"
python3 -B tests/box3d_web/replay/browser.py \
  --export-record "$NEW_EXPORT/report.json" --out "$NEW_PAIR" --ticks 120

Use absolute tool/library paths and fresh output directories. Build the selected Web archive with build/build_box3d.sh WebSIMD CACHE. Existing web Node dependencies must be available. These commands execute local builds and browsers.

The optional godot4.7.1-web-dlink-rtc-scratch-v1 profile derives a custom template from the exact pinned official web_dlink_release.zip. It changes only the binary RTC send bridge in godot.js: one 64 KiB buffer per engine JavaScript module replaces fresh packet backing buffers and byte-at-a-time copies. Text, oversized, invalid-range and nested sends retain the original path. Both engine Wasm files and every other template entry stay byte-identical.

Shell
python3 -B build/web_rtc_template.py derive \
  --source "$GODOT_WEB_TEMPLATE" --out "$NEW_TEMPLATE"
python3 -B tests/box3d_web/replay/export.py \
  --out "$NEW_EXPORT" --native-library "$NATIVE_LIBRARY" \
  --web-archive "$WEB_ARCHIVE" --odin "$ODIN" --godot "$GODOT" --emcc "$EMCC" \
  --web-template-record "$NEW_TEMPLATE/template-record.json"

Derivation creates a new ZIP and provenance record. Selection happens before ordinary import/export through Godot's custom-template setting. The helper verifies the pinned source, transformation and all payloads; it preserves installed templates and existing outputs. Without the explicit record argument, the export command uses its existing template settings. Template byte checks and isolated RTC copy tests are separate from actual game frame qualification.

The pair requires actual nonzero committed controls from both seats, one accepted boost action and applied outcome per seat, two confirmed boost effects per browser, signature-checked correction, byte equality of Solver/Game/Side/Observations/ Occurrences, the application's actual terminal signature acknowledgement, measured SDK cleanup and the real Core shutdown marker. Replay Side is legitimately empty. Large keys and pointers stay in typed Odin/C values; the final frame crosses the console as exact base64 bytes with hexadecimal hashes.

This is a functional software-GL check: render=0 disables 3D drawing while the same input, physics, copied presentation and network callbacks run. Chrome uses the existing RTC harness's local-IP discovery flag. It establishes neither a rendering budget nor default-browser Internet connectivity. The original rendered software-GL remote-input failure and mDNS connection failures remain retained. Foreground rendering, Internet/TURN and other browsers have separate roadmap work.

SAMPLE_NETWORK reports actual committed action counts, outcomes and cue delivery. Its latest planned/executed physics repair and live configured limit are separate from Stats.replay_max_depth: that legacy timing field is not populated by the complete physics path, so its zero is not a maximum-depth measurement. Final-frame bytes, raw console rows, process arguments and export hashes are retained.

recovery.py reuses the small adapter fixture runner for a separate browser test:

Shell
python3 -B tests/box3d_web/replay/recovery.py \
  --out "$NEW_RECOVERY" --native-library "$NATIVE_LIBRARY" \
  --web-archive "$WEB_ARCHIVE" --odin "$ODIN" --godot "$GODOT" --emcc "$EMCC" --execute

Its real Core/Meter-owned Server and Client use the public Memory transport. The receiver consumes and discards actual packets while the authority progresses beyond H128, then resumes normal delivery. The oracle requires an actual recovery notice, newer validated Welcome scope/baseline, complete five-part equality, continued Native work and checked cleanup. Original world/catalog creators are destroyed before the recovery. This receiver-discard test does not model SCTP, WebRTC reliable loss or an Internet outage. Without --execute it writes a plan.

Current scoped evidence is in report.json. Native/web cross-play, room authorization, rejoin/observer UX and match-length performance are not qualified by this report.
